ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $O$ is a point on the straight line $AB$. An arbitrary ray $OM$ passes through $O$, $OC$ bisects $\angle AOM$, and $OD$ bisects $\angle BOM$. What is the measure of $\angle COD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $OC$ bisects $\angle AOM$ and $OD$ bisects $\angle BOM$, \\
thus $\angle MOC= \frac{1}{2}\angle AOM$ and $\angle MOD= \frac{1}{2}\angle BOM$, \\
hence $\angle COD=\angle MOC+\angle MOD= \frac{1}{2}\angle AOM+\frac{1}{2}\angle BOM=\frac{1}{2}(\angle AOM+\angle BOM)=\frac{1}{2}\times 180^\circ=\boxed{90^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A, O, B are on the same horizontal straight line, with O located between A and B; from O, three rays are drawn upward, pointing respectively to C at the upper left, to M at the upper right and relatively steep, and to D at the upper right and relatively flat. Therefore ∠AOM and ∠MOB together form the straight angle ∠AOB. Reasoning: Let ∠AOM = x. Because OA and OB are opposite rays on one straight line, ∠AOM + ∠MOB = 180°, that is, ∠MOB = 180° − x. According to the problem statement, OC bisects ∠AOM, so ∠COM = x/2; OD bisects ∠BOM, so ∠MOD = (180° − x)/2. From the order in the figure, ∠COD is obtained by adding ∠COM and ∠MOD, therefore ∠COD = x/2 + (180° − x)/2 = 180°/2 = 90°.
